headline: Judiciary says they carried out operations for Israel and the US and damaged a Karaj electricity substation
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- executions carried out] Iran executed three men on Sunday Nov 8: Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- judiciary] They were convicted of taking part in armed unrest during the January 2026 protests and carrying out operations for Israel and the US;…
sources: Iranian judiciary / state media (Fars News Agency; Mizan Online), via Reuters; Al Jazeera liveblog 05:15 GMT
fault_line: Justice for arson and attacks on the state -- or a regime executing protesters to frighten the next uprising?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- executions carried out] Iran executed three men on Sunday Nov 8: Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- judiciary] They were convicted of taking part in armed unrest during the January 2026 protests and carrying out operations for Israel and the US; accused of using firearms, grenades and Molotov cocktails, setting fire to public facilities and damaging an electricity substation in Karaj, causing power outages. Dioband was arrested Jan 11; ten others were arrested under his supervision; the three were sentenced to death with assets confiscated; the Supreme Court upheld the sentences; other defendants received 5-10 year prison terms. [CORROBORATED -- HRANA] Human Rights Activists News Agency independently documented death sentences for Hamid Kazemi and 'Hassan Divand' (spelling variant of Dioband) by Branch 2 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court. [CONTEXT -- AJ liveblog] UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk urged Iranian authorities to halt all executions and move toward abolishing the death penalty. [ALLEGATION -- judiciary's framing, unproven] That the three carried out operations 'for Israel and the US' -- no independent evidence presented in the reporting.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families: Reuters (T1 wire, 04:41Z, reporting state media), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2, STATE QA, 05:15 GMT, citing Fars), Times of Israel (T3, 04:44Z). Straits Times and The Print carry the same Reuters wire (1 family, not counted separately). Fars News Agency has NO declared tier in the registry -- reported with attribution, never counted toward corroboration. HRANA (rights monitor) independently confirms the death sentences for two of the three. TRAP AVOIDED: a separate March 2026 execution set (three men hanged in Qom for killing two police officers, Reuters Mar 19) and a separate July Isfahan public-hanging case are different events -- not conflated.
sections.what_disputed: Rights groups contest the fairness of the process: HRANA documents the sentences but the trials are described by rights monitors as unfair, with torture/coerced-confession allegations in protest-linked cases generally (e.g. July Isfahan case, Rights Atlas/ABC). UN rights chief said at least 27 people in protest-linked cases had been executed since Mar 19 (per Rights Atlas, Aug). The 'operations for Israel and the US' charge is the judiciary's attribution, not independently evidenced. Spelling discrepancy: Reuters/Fars 'Dioband' vs HRANA 'Divand'.
sections.why_matters: While the war fills the headlines, Tehran is hanging January's protesters -- three more today, named, for 'operations for Israel and the US'. The charge is the regime's; the hangings are confirmed.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Reuters published 2026-11-08T04:41:00Z = 08:41 , inside the 0900 window but missed by the 0900 scan; AJ liveblog entry 05:15 GMT = 09:15 , IN-WINDOW) -- Iran executes three men over January 2026 protest unrest: Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi, Reza Zanganeh; judiciary says they carried out operations for Israel and the US and damaged a Karaj electricity substation

totw_analysis: Our read: While the war fills the headlines, Tehran is hanging January's protesters -- three more today, named, for 'operations for Israel and the US'. The charge is the regime's; the hangings are confirmed. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Justice for arson and attacks on the state -- or a regime executing protesters to frighten the next uprising?
